findings.source_passage: as though a white man were anything more dignified than a whitewashed negro
findings.why_it_matters: The draft buries this in a compressed clause ('jeered at our companionship, as though a white man were anything more dignified than a whitewashed negro') without preserving the full setup about how the narrator and Queequeg 'did not notice the jeering glances' while absorbed in the scene—the irony of their obliviousness is part of the signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the framing: they were so full of the reeling scene they did not notice the jeering glances, then deliver the 'whitewashed negro' line with its full context.

findings.source_passage: "Capting! Capting!" yelled the bumpkin, running towards that officer; "Capting, Capting, here's the devil."
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Capting! here's the devil' exchange and the captain's exact threat ('I'll kill-e you, you cannibal') are comic-voice highlights that critics cite; the draft collapses the entire back-and-forth into 'The Captain stormed,' erasing Melville's dialect comedy entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum the bumpkin's 'here's the devil' cry and the captain's 'I'll kill-e you, you cannibal' retort, which sets up the Queequeg dialect response that the draft does preserve.

findings.source_passage: Grace being said,—for those people have their grace as well as we—though Queequeg told me that unlike us, who at such times look downwards to our platters, they, on the contrary, copying the ducks, glance upwards to the great Giver of all feasts
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Upon this, he told me another story'
findings.why_it_matters: This aside is interpretively central: it performs Melville's cultural relativism—the 'savages' having grace, and a more spiritually upward-gazing form of it—which is a recurring critical touchstone for the novel's anti-ethnocentrism. The draft omits it entirely, jumping straight to the captain washing his hands.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the grace parenthesis before the captain's blunder; it is brief and carries heavy interpretive weight that justifies the words.

findings.source_passage: the world-wandering whale ships lay silent and safely moored at last; while from others came a sound of carpenters and coopers, with blended noises of fires and forges
findings.why_it_matters: The contrast between the silent resting ships and the active forges—one voyage ending, another beginning—is compressed to a mere list; the poetic rhythm of the passage is lost though the idea survives.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'world-wandering whale ships lay silent and safely moored' phrase alongside the forges detail to maintain the rhythmic contrast.

summary: Three medium-severity failures—erasure of the 'Capting! here's the devil' dialect comedy, loss of the culturally-relativist grace-at-the-feast aside, and the flattened captain-exchange that strips Queequeg's defining 'kill-e big whale' retort of its setup—together trigger regeneration.
